correctness.rationale: The minimum identifying-code state space is precisely the 584 size-eight sets on the explicitly labeled GP(8,3), determined by all nonempty closed-neighborhood signatures and all 120 pairwise signature differences. An independent fresh checker tested all 65,536 masks, recovered exactly 584 size-eight feasible masks, then independently generated all single-vertex exchanges and distinguished host-adjacent slides from unrestricted jumps. It reproduced 864 slide edges, one 488-state component and 96 singletons, slide diameter 10, and degrees 0:96,2:240,4:168,6:48,8:30,24:2. It also reproduced 2496 jump edges, a connected graph of diameter 8 and radius 7, jump degrees 4:96,6:48,8:48,9:192,10:144,12:48,24:8; frozen host-edge classes 5:48 and 7:48. Exhaustive code and move rules prove finite completeness.

value.rationale: PASS: identifying-code reconfiguration is a motivated graph-theoretic robustness/relocation question, and the complete optimum-state graph of the canonical 16-vertex cubic symmetric Möbius–Kantor graph is a naturally bounded exact invariant. The contrast between connected unrestricted jumps and 96 frozen adjacent slides, with sharp distance data, is independently useful even without a larger graph-family theorem.

limitations: All counts are labeled, not modulo automorphism; code size is fixed at the previously known optimum eight.
Independent checks did not compare byte-for-byte with supplied jumps.txt/slides.txt, but regenerated host, states and all move invariants independently.
